markdown_report:
At 20% progress, prioritize a controlled extension: **padding-invariant GRU4Rec with absolute-event-recency-weighted BPR-max**. Its intended user benefits are fewer weak thematic/functional matches and less emphasis on older, occasional interests. Neither benefit is established yet.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) All four reported padding errors exceed 1e-5. Encoding correctness therefore precedes interpreting temporal effects. (2) Movies and Electronics have sampled wrong-order rates of 6.25% and 5.90%. Competitive-negative training targets this measured weakness without proving full-catalog improvement. (3) Absolute event age survives cropping. Window position can assign different weights to the same event.

**Insights from related work.** (1) GRU4Rec’s BPR-max emphasizes competitive negatives [1]. Its negative-score penalty is a separate intervention. (2) MTAM motivates temporal modeling [2]. Learned temporal gates add complexity before recency weighting has demonstrated value here. (3) RepeatNet distinguishes repetition from exploration [3]. Its direct repeat mechanism does not transfer directly to unseen-item recommendations.

The framework separates **encoding correctness → ranking discrimination → temporal supervision → optional retention architecture**. Padding verification is a prerequisite; ranking and weighting require separate controls; temporal gates remain a later direction.

Three candidate ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/code difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Dimension-specific assessment: positive; negative |
|---|---|---|
| A. Absolute-event weighting plus BPR-max [1] | 3/7/7/8/4 | Originality: controlled combination; established components. Potential: interpretable foundation; possibly small gains. User: targets weak matches and stale interests; cannot establish compatibility. Model: targets weak margins; sampled improvement may not generalize. Difficulty: training-only change; absolute indices require integration. |
| B. Time-gap-conditioned GRU retention [2] | 5/7/7/6/7 | Originality: contextual retention; existing precedent. Potential: adaptive intent; sparse timestamps may limit learning. User: emphasizes current behavior; elapsed time cannot reveal satisfied needs. Model: alters context use; current sensitivity evidence is confounded. Difficulty: one network; recurrence and predictor changes are substantial. |
| C. Recurrence-conditioned input gate [3] | 4/6/6/5/6 | Originality: unseen-item adaptation; repetition modeling exists. Potential: distinguishes persistence; repeats may be scarce. User: addresses repeated versus occasional interests; ownership remains ambiguous. Model: testable context behavior; no measured recurrence-specific failure. Difficulty: compact gate; prefix-only recurrence accounting needs care. |

Select A for feasibility. First verify padding invariance against unpadded executions; repair only if necessary. Compare baseline loss and BPR-max under uniform weighting before enabling bounded absolute-event weights. Keep negative count and score penalty fixed during this comparison, then vary each separately if budget permits.

Use unchanged four-category routing, splits, seeds, training limits and host validation. Deploy one checkpoint per category, preserve diagnostic interfaces, and update the predictor writer whenever inference changes. Select solely by macro validation HR@10; report diagnostic changes as supporting evidence. No validation gain is claimed.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03847; [2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08598; [3] https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/4408.

idea.description: Evaluate absolute-event-recency-weighted BPR-max within the supplied corrected GRU4Rec, retaining exactly one independently trained model per category. Treat padding invariance as a prerequisite and separate objective, weighting, negative-count and negative-score-penalty changes.
idea.motivation: The proposal explicitly targets two reported user-facing failures: broad but weak matches crowding out closer choices, and older or occasional interests outweighing recent behavior. Competitive-negative ranking targets the measured weak sampled separation in Movies_and_TV and Electronics. Padding verification addresses the reported model-facing inconsistency across all four categories. These are mechanisms to test, not demonstrated improvements or evidence of product compatibility, purchase readiness or satisfied needs.
idea.implementation_notes:
Integrate into the supplied baseline rather than reconstructing unspecified preprocessing or configuration. Preserve its GRU backbone, optimizer, scoring transformation, sequence length, batch size and checkpoint-selection schedule during initial comparisons. Use preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; all artifacts remain beneath the trial directory. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing.

Before training changes, compare eval-mode valid features and candidate scores against individual unpadded executions, including empty rows, varied lengths, batch permutations and added leading padding. If necessary, compact real tokens, pack only nonempty rows, run the existing GRU, unpack and scatter features to their original positions. Preserve existing output transformations and zero padding outputs. Read the maximum nonpadding index, never count-1; preserve explicit empty-history handling. Make identical changes in the predictor writer and diagnostics.

For the BPR-max arm, initially use K=16 negatives and zero negative-score penalty. Sample uniformly with replacement from real item IDs excluding the target and complete observed training history; never use held-out labels for filtering. Skip and count positions without eligible negatives. This sampling specification is an adaptation rather than an official GRU4Rec sampler reproduction. Use stable log_softmax plus logsumexp, retain gradients through negative softmax weights, and do not divide BPR-max by K. If the original loss cannot use identical negative tensors without changing its definition, disclose the sampling confound and retain an unchanged baseline control.

For a target at absolute zero-based training-history index t, define distance=T-1-t and weight a=0.5+0.5*exp(-distance/10). Carry t through the internal sampler; do not derive it from crop position. Preserve the baseline reduction: for a global mean over valid positions, use sum(a*loss)/sum(a); for a per-user/window mean, normalize within that same unit before the inherited outer reduction. Weighting may change effective user contribution and does not guarantee equal-user exposure. Log contribution by history length and effective sample size. Keep window-position weighting as an explicitly different optional control.

Order comparisons as unchanged baseline, verified encoding with baseline objective if repair was needed, uniform BPR-max, then recency-weighted BPR-max. Reserve further experiments for negative count and negative-score penalty separately. Use matched initialization, sampling streams, validation cadence and update limits where applicable; record actual GPU time because compute cost differs. Prespecify an affordable sequence within the shared 43,200 GPU-second allowance, including failures and diagnostics.

Maintain sample_batch and ModelView contracts, including view.model as the trained nn.Module, item_emb, aligned B x L log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Public diagnostic batches remain (None, sequence, positive, negative); absolute indices use an internal side channel. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), incorporating measured values and definitions. Unavailable metadata and simulator traits stay unavailable.

Select solely through the unchanged host macro validation HR@10 protocol. Each category loads one selected checkpoint with matching architecture and scoring; no fusion or checkpoint averaging. Preserve full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for the twenty designated training users. Use only allowed public data and no hidden test files, other-trial artifacts, pretrained weights or additional datasets.
idea.pseudocode:
set_preprocessing_seed(0)
set_training_seed(42)
# Integration pseudocode; inherit the supplied baseline's data and configuration.
for category in REQUIRED_FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    model = supplied_corrected_GRU4Rec()
    verify_padding_invariance_or_repair_consistently(model, predictor_writer)
    for epoch in range(max_epochs_at_most_200):
        for step in range(200):
            batch = internal_sample_batch_with_absolute_target_indices()
            features = model.log2feats(batch.sequence)
            valid = (batch.sequence != 0) & (batch.positive != 0)
            negatives, eligible = sample_training_filtered_uniform_negatives(K=16)
            valid &= eligible
            if not valid.any():
                continue
            # Score only valid positions to avoid undefined masked losses.
            pos = score_with_existing_transformation(features[valid], batch.positive[valid])
            neg = score_K_with_existing_transformation(features[valid], negatives[valid])
            log_mix = log_softmax(neg, dim=-1)
            loss = -logsumexp(log_mix + logsigmoid(pos[..., None] - neg), dim=-1)
            # Initial negative-score penalty is zero.
            if recency_arm:
                distance = batch.full_training_length[valid_rows] - 1 - batch.absolute_target_index[valid]
                weights = 0.5 + 0.5 * exp(-distance / 10.0)
            else:
                weights = ones_like(loss)
            loss = weighted_reduction_preserving_baseline_units(loss, weights, batch, valid)
            inherited_optimizer_step(loss)
        validate_at_inherited_schedule()
    save_one_selected_checkpoint_and_matching_configuration(category)
write_matching_predictor_with_four_category_routing()
# Run controls separately; never combine their predictions.
# Final readout uses maximum nonpadding index with explicit empty-row handling.

originality.positive: Separates absolute-event recency from window position and isolates ranking, weighting, negative count and score regularization in a diagnosis-driven GRU4Rec experiment.
originality.negative: BPR-max, bounded recency weighting and padding-invariant recurrent execution are established techniques.

future_potential.positive: Provides a feasible foundation for determining whether competitive ranking and recent-target supervision justify later temporal retention changes.
future_potential.negative: No supplied experiment establishes an improvement, and recency weighting cannot directly model compatibility or whether ownership satisfies a need.

code_difficulty.positive: The main intervention changes training loss and target weights while preserving inference architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Absolute target indices, efficient training-history exclusions, inherited reduction semantics and consistent padding handling require careful baseline integration.

related_work.title: Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains for Session-based Recommendations
contributions: Introduces ranking-max objectives, including BPR-max, for recurrent recommendation.
Provides direct motivation for emphasizing high-scoring negative competitors.
limitations: Does not establish gains under the supplied Amazon splits and pinned evaluation.
Changing sampling or score transformations alongside the loss would confound attribution.

related_work.title: MTAM
contributions: The supplied search summary describes temporal gates and historical memory for recurrent sequential recommendation.
Motivates a later experiment on time-conditioned GRU retention.
limitations: Its reported mechanisms do not validate the proposed recency-weighted objective.
A recurrence change requires matching predictor and diagnostic adaptations.

related_work.title: RepeatNet
contributions: Explicitly distinguishes repeat consumption from exploration.
Motivates examining observed recurrence as evidence about persistent interests.
limitations: Direct repeat-item prediction has limited applicability to unseen-item recommendation.
Repeated interactions do not establish purchase readiness or unmet needs.
